q: If a : b : c = 3 : 4 : 7, then the ratio (a + b + c) : c is equal to
s: $$\begin{aligned} &\,\,\,\, {\text{ }}a{\text{ }}:{\text{ }}b{\text{ }}:{\text{ }}c \\ &\,\,\,\, {\text{ }}3{\text{ }}:{\text{ }}4{\text{ }}:{\text{ }}7{\text{ }} \\ & \boxed{\,\,3x:4x:7x\,\,\,\,} \Rightarrow 14x \\ & \therefore a + b + c = 14x \\ & c = 7x \\ & \therefore \left( {a + b + c} \right):c \\ & = 14x:7x \\ & = 2:1 \end{aligned}$$

q: The number of students in 3 classes is in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. If 12 students are increased in each class this ratio changes to 8 : 11 : 14. The total number of students in the three classes in the beginning was
s: Let the number of students in the classes be 2x, 3x and 4x respectively; Total students = 2x + 3x + 4x = 9x $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{According}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{question}}, \\ & \frac{{ {2x + 12} }}{{ {3x + 12} }} = \frac{8}{{11}} \\ & or,\,24x + 96 = 22x + 132 \\ & or,\,2x = 132 - 96 \\ & or,\,x = \frac{{36}}{2} = 18 \\ & {\text{Hence,}} \\ & {\text{Original}}\,{\text{number}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{students}}, \\ & 9x = 9 \times 18 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 162 \end{aligned}$$

q: A box has 210 coins of denominations one-rupee and fifty paise only. The ratio of their respective values is 13 : 11. The number of one-rupee coin is
s: Respective ratio of the NUMBER of coins; = 13 : 11 × 2 = 13 : 22 Hence, Number of 1 rupee coins; = $$\frac{{13 \times 210}}{{13 + 22}}$$ = 78

q: If $$\frac{2}{3}$$ of A=75% of B = 0.6 of C, then A : B : C is
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{According}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{thequestion,}} \\ & {\frac{{2A}}{3}} = {\frac{{75B}}{{100}}} = {\frac{{C \times 6}}{{10}}} \\ & {\text{Above}}\,{\text{relation}}\,{\text{gives}}; \\ & \frac{{A \times 2}}{3} = \frac{{B \times 3}}{4} \\ & \to \frac{A}{B} = \frac{9}{8} \\ & {\text{And}}, \\ & \frac{{B \times 3}}{4} = \frac{{C \times 3}}{5} \\ & \to \frac{B}{C} = 4:5 \\ & \to \frac{B}{C} = 8:10 {\text{ (multiple by 2)}} \\ & {\text{Thus,}} \\ & A:B:C = 9:8:10 \end{aligned}$$

q: If A and B are in the ratio 3 : 4, and B and C in the ratio 12 : 13, then A and C will be in the ratio
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\frac{A}{B}} \times {\frac{B}{C}} = {\frac{3}{4}} \times {\frac{{12}}{{13}}} \\ & Or,\,\frac{A}{C} = \frac{{36}}{{52}} = 9:13 \end{aligned}$$

q: The salaries of A, B and C are in the ratio 1 : 3 : 4. If the salaries are increased by 5%, 10% and 15% respectively, then the increased salaries will be in the ratio
s: Let A's Salary = Rs. 100 Then, B's Salary = Rs. 300 And, C's Salary = Rs. 400 Salary has given in 1 : 3 : 4 ratio Now, 5% increase in A's Salary, A's new Salary = (100 + 5% of 100) = Rs. 105 B's Salary increases by 10%, Then, B's new Salary = (300 + 10% of 300) = Rs. 330 C's Salary increases by 15%, C's new Salary = (400 + 15% of 400) = Rs. 460 Then, ratio of increased Salary, A : B : C = 105 : 330 : 460 = 21 : 66 : 92 Alternative 100 (A's salary) === 5%↑ ===> 105(A's increased salary) 300 (B's salary) === 10%↑ ===> 330 (B's increased salary) 400 (C's salary) === 15%↑ ===> 460 (C's increased salary) Ratio of their increased salary = 105 : 330 : 460 = 21 : 66 : 92

q: If A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5 then A : B : C is
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{\text{A}}}{{\text{B}}} = \frac{2}{3} \\ & \frac{{\text{B}}}{{\text{C}}} = \frac{4}{5} \end{aligned}$$ A : B : C = 2 × 4 : 3 × 4 : 3 × 5 = 8 : 12 : 15

q: If two times A is equal to three times of B and also equal to four times of C, then A : B : C is
In a school having roll strength 286, the ratio of boys and girls is 8 : 5. If 22 more girls get admitted into the school, the ratio of boys and girls becomes

q: Two numbers are in ratio 4 : 5 and their LCM is 180. The smaller number is
s: Let two numbers be 4x and 5x Their LCM = 180 and HCF = x Now, 1 st number × 2 nd number = LCM × HCF Or, 4x × 5x = 180 × x Or, 20x = 180 Or, x = 9 Then, the smaller number = 4 × 9 = 36

q: If A : B = 2 : 3, B : C = 4 : 5 and C : D = 5 : 9 then A : D is equal to:
In a class, the number of girls is 20% more than that of the boys. The strength of the class is 66. If 4 more girls are admitted to the class, the ratio of the number of boys to that of the girls is
s: Girls : boys = 6 : 5 Hence, girls = $$6 \times \frac{{66}}{{11}}$$ = 36 Boys = 30 New ratio, 30 : (36 + 4) = 3 : 4

q: What must be added to each term of the ratio 7 : 11, So as to make it equal to 3 : 4?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let }}x{\text{ be added to each term}}. \\ & {\text{According to question}}, \\ & \frac{{ {7 + x} }}{{11 + x}} = \frac{3}{4} \\ & Or,\,33 + 3x = 28 + 4x \\ & Or,\,x = 5 \end{aligned}$$

q: Two numbers are in ratio 7 : 11. If 7 is added to each of the numbers, the ratio becomes 2 : 3. The smaller number is
s: Let the numbers be 7x and 11x. $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{According to question}}, \\ & \frac{{ {7x + 7} }}{{ {11x + 7} }} = \frac{2}{3} \\ & Or,\,22x + 14 = 21x + 21 \\ & Or,\,x = 7 \\ & {\text{Smaller}}\,{\text{number}} = 49 \end{aligned}$$

q: Two numbers are in ratio P : Q. when 1 is added to both the numerator and the denominator, the ratio gets changed to $$\frac{{\text{R}}}{{\text{S}}}$$. again, when 1 is added to both the numerator and denominator, it becomes $$\frac{1}{2}$$. Find the sum of P and Q.
s: If we go through normal method, It will be quite cumbersome,so, We will solve this question through options Taking Option A: It has P + Q = 3. The possible value of $$\frac{{\text{P}}}{{\text{Q}}}$$ is $$\frac{1}{2}$$ or $$\frac{2}{1}$$ Using $$\frac{1}{2}$$, we see that on adding 2 in both the numerator and denominator we get $$\frac{3}{4}$$ (not required value) Similarly we check for $$\frac{2}{1}$$, this will also not give the required value Option B: We have $$\frac{1}{3}$$ possible ratio Then, we get the final value as $$\frac{3}{5}$$ (not = to $$\frac{1}{2}$$) Hence, rejected Option C: Here we have $$\frac{1}{4}$$ or $$\frac{2}{3}$$ Checking for $$\frac{1}{4}$$ we get $$\frac{3}{6}$$ = $$\frac{1}{2}$$ Hence, the option c is correct

q: The ratio of water and milk in a 30 liter mixture is 7 : 3. Find the quantity of water to be added to the mixture in order to make this ratio 6 : 1.
s: Here,Let water = 7x and milk = 3x Now, 7x + 3x = 30 x = 3 So, water = 7x = 7 × 3 = 21 liter Milk = 3x = 3 × 3 = 9 liter Now, we keep milk constant and add water to mixture to get ratio 6 : 1 Let water in this mixture = 6y and milk = y We have, milk = 9 liter, so y = 9 liter Water = 6y = 6 × 9 = 54 liter Then extra water to be added is 33 liter

q: The incomes of A and B are in the ratio 3 : 2 and their expenditure are in ratio 5 : 3. If each saves Rs. 1000, then, A's income can be:
s: Let income of A and B be 3x and 2x respectively. Also, their expenditure is 5y and 3y. Now, according to question, 3x - 5y = 1000 ------- (i) × 3 2x - 3y = 1000 ---------- (ii) × 5 9x - 15y - 10x + 15y = 3000 - 5000 Or, -x = -2000 Or, x = 2000 Then, income of A = 3x = 3 × 2000 = Rs. 6000

q: The difference between two positive numbers is 10 and the ratio between them is 5 : 3. Find the product of the two numbers.
s: Let the two positive numbers be 5x and 3x respectively According to question, 5x - 3x = 10 Or, x = 5Then numbers are 25 and 15 Thus, their product = 25 × 15 = 375

q: If 30 oxen can plough $$\frac{1}{7}$$ th of a field in 2 days, how many days 18 oxen will take to do the remaining work?
s: We will use work equivalence method, $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{30}}{{18}} = \frac{{ {\frac{1}{7}} }}{{ {\frac{6}{7}} }} \times \frac{x}{2} \\ & \frac{5}{3} = {\frac{1}{6}} \times \frac{x}{2} \\ & Or,\,x = \frac{{60}}{3} = 20\,{\text{days}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A cat leaps 5 leaps for every 4 leaps of a dog, but 3 leaps of the dog are equal to 4 leaps of the cat. What is the ratio of the speed of the cat to that of the dog?
s: Given; 3dog = 4 cat Or, $$\frac{{{\text{dog}}}}{{{\text{cat}}}} = \frac{4}{3}$$ Let cat's 1 leap = 3 meter and dogs 1 leap = 4 meter Then, ratio of speed of cat and dog = $$\frac{{3 \times 5}}{{4 \times 4}}$$ = 15 : 16

q: The present ratio of ages of A and B is 4 : 5. 18 years ago, this ratio was 11 : 16. Find the sum total of their present ages.
s: Let present age of A and B be 4x and 5x 18 years ago their ages $$\frac{{4x - 18}}{{5x - 18}} = \frac{{11}}{{16}}$$ Or, 64x - 288 = 55x - 198 Or, 64x - 55x = -198 + 288 Or, 9x = 90 Or, x = $$\frac{{90}}{9}$$ = 10 Sum of the present ages = 40 + 50 = 90 years

q: A dishonest milk man mixed 1 liter of water for every 3 liters of milk and thus made up 36 liters of milk. If he now adds 15 liters of milk to mixture, find the ratio of milk and water in the new mixture:
s: Quantity of milk and water in the 36 liter mixture 27 liter milk and 9 liter water Now, 15 liters milk is added then milk becomes 42 liters Now, ratio = 42 : 9 = 14 : 3

q: If the ratio of the ages of Maya and Chhaya is 6 : 5 at present, and fifteen years from now, the ratio will get changed to 9 : 8, then find Maya's present age.
s: Let Maya's and Chhaya's present age is 6x and 5x respectively And, $$\frac{{6{\text{x}} + 15}}{{5{\text{x}} + 15}} = \frac{9}{8}$$ Or, 48x + 120 = 45x = 135 Or, 3x = 15 Or, x = 5 Present age of Maya = 6x = 30

q: The Lucknow-Indore Express without its rake can go 24 km an hour, and the speed is diminished by a quantity that varies as the square root of the number of wagon attached. If it is known that with four wagons its speed is 20 km/h, the greatest number of wagons with which the engine can just move is
s: Speed = $$24 - {\text{k}}\sqrt {\text{n}}$$ Putting the value, n = 4 we get, k = 2 Now the equation (as k = 2) become, S = $$24 - {\text{k}}\sqrt {\text{n}}$$ Thus, it means when n = 144, speed will be zero. Hence, train can just move when 143 wagons are attached

q: If x varies as y then x 2 + y 2 varies as
s: Given, x = y Or, x - y = 0 Or, (x - y) 2 = 0 Or, x 2 + y 2 - 2xy = 0 Or, x 2 + y 2 = 2xy It means that, x 2 + y 2 varies as xy

q: Brindavan Express leave Chennai Central Station every day at 07.50 am and goes to Bangalore City Railway station. This train is very popular among the travelers. On 25th July 2012 number of passengers traveling by I class and II class was in the ratio 1 : 4. The fare for this travel is in the ratio 3 : 1. The total fare collected was Rs. 224000. (Rs. Two lakhs twenty four thousand only). What was the fare collected from I class passengers on that day?
s: Let the number of passenger traveling by first class be x Then, number of passenger traveling by second class will be 4x But the fare is in the ratio 3 : 1 In other words, if 3y fare is collected per I class passenger, y would be collected per II class passenger Fares of I class passengers : Fares of II class passengers = x × 3y : 4x × y = 3 : 4 The above ratio can be interpreted as follows If total fare is 3 + 4 = 7, then I class passengers should pay Rs. 3 Similarly, we can calculate the fare of I class passengers when total was 224000 Total Fare Class Fare 7 3 224000 ? = $$224000 \times \frac{3}{7}$$ = Rs. 96000

q: A vessel of capacity 2 litre has 25% alcohol and another vessel of capacity 6 litre had 40% alcohol. The total liquid of 8 litre was poured out in a vessel of capacity 10 litre and thus the rest part of the vessel was filled with the water. what is the new concentration of mixture ?
s: Amount of alcohol in first vessel, = 25% of 2 litre = 0.25 × 2 = 0.5 litre Amount of alcohol in second vessel, = 40% of 6 litre = 0.4 × 6 = 2.4 litre Total amount of alcohol out of 10 litres of mixture is 0.5 + 2.4 = 2.9 litre Thus, Concentration of the mixture is, $$\frac{{2.9 \times 100}}{{10}}$$ = 29%

q: The number of oranges in three basket are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. In which ratio the no. of oranges in first two basket must be increased so that the new ratio becomes 5 : 4 : 3 ?
s: Let, B 1 : B 2 : B 3 = 3x : 4x : 5x and B 1 : B 2 : B 3 = 5y : 4y : 3y Number of oranges remain constant in third basket as increase in oranges takes place only in first two baskets. Hence, 5x = 3y x = $$\frac{3y}{5}$$ and, ∴ 3x : 4x : 5x (putting the vale of x) = $$\frac{{9{\text{y}}}}{5}:\frac{{{\text{12y}}}}{5}:\frac{{{\text{15y}}}}{5}$$ = 9y : 12y : 15y And, 5y : 4y : 3y (multiple by 5) → 25y : 20y : 15y ∴Increment in first basket = 16 And, Increment in second basket = 8 Thus, Required ratio = $$\frac{{16}}{8}$$ = 2 : 1

q: At a casino in Mumbai, there are 3 tables A, B and C. The payoffs at A is 10 : 1, at B is 20 : 1 and C is 30 :1. If a man bets Rs. 200 at each table and win at two of the tables, what is the maximum and minimum difference between his earnings can be ?
s: Maximum earning will be only possible when he will won on the maximum yielding table A → 10 : 1 B → 20 : 1 C → 30 : 1 i.e., he won B and C but lost on A 20 × 200 + 30 × 200 - 1 × 200 = 9800 Minimum earnings will be when he won on table A and B and lose on table 3 10 × 200 + 20 × 200 - 1 × 200 = 5800 Therefore, difference = 9800 - 5800 = Rs. 4000 Alternatively, The difference, = [(30 + 20 - 1) - (10 + 20 -1)] × 200 = Rs. 4000

q: A track covers a distance of 550 metres in 1 minute whereas a bus covers a distance of 33 kms in 45 minute. The ratio of their speeds is:
s: Speed of track = 550 per minute. Speed of bus = $$\frac{{33\,{\text{kms}}}}{{45}}$$ = $$\frac{{33000}}{{45}}$$ = 733.33 m/minute Ratio of their speeds = $$\frac{{550}}{{733.33}}$$ = 3 : 4

q: Total number of men, women and children working in a factory is 18. They earn Rs. 4000 in a day. If the sum of the wages of all men, all women and all children is in ratio of 18 : 10 : 12 and if the wages of an individual man, woman and child is in ratio 6 : 5 : 3, then how much a woman earn in a day?
s: Ratio of number of men, women and children, $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{18}}{6}:\frac{{10}}{5}:\frac{{12}}{3} \\ & = 3:2:4 \end{aligned}$$ Total (Men + Women + Children) = 18 3X + 2X + 4X = 18 9X = 18 X = 2 Hence, number of women = 2X = 2 × 2 = 4 Share of all women = $$\frac{{10 \times 4000}}{{40}}$$ = Rs. 1000 [18 + 10 + 12 = 40] Thus, share of each woman = $$\frac{{1000}}{4}$$ = Rs. 250

q: A and B are two alloys in which ratios of gold and copper are 5 : 3 and 5 : 11 respectively. If these equally amount of two alloys are melted and made alloy C. What will be the ratio of gold and copper in alloy C?
s: Ratio of Gold and Copper in Alloy A = 5 : 3 Ratio of Gold and Copper in Alloy B = 5 : 11 Amount of Gold in Alloy A = $$\frac{5}{8}$$ Amount of Gold In Alloy B = $$\frac{5}{{16}}$$ Amount of Copper in A = $$\frac{3}{8}$$ Amount of Copper in B = $$\frac{{11}}{{16}}$$ Amount of Gold In C, = (Amount of gold in A + Amount of gold in B) = $$\frac{5}{8}$$ + $$\frac{5}{{16}}$$ = $$\frac{{10 + 5}}{{16}}$$ = $$\frac{{15}}{{16}}$$ Amount of Copper in C, = Amount of Copper in A + Amount of Copper in B = $$\frac{3}{8}$$ + $$\frac{{11}}{{16}}$$ = $$\frac{{17}}{{16}}$$ So, Ratio of Gold and Copper in C, $$= \frac{{15}}{{16}}:\frac{{17}}{{16}} = 15:17$$

q: A bag contains an equal number of one rupee, 50 paise and 25 paise coins. If the total value is Rs. 35, how many coins of each type are there?
s: Let X coins of each type of there Total Value = Rs. 35 Now, X + $$\frac{{\text{X}}}{2}$$ + $$\frac{{\text{X}}}{4}$$ = 35 4X + 2X + X = 140 7X = 140 X = 20

q: A bucket contains a mixture of two liquids A and B in the proportion 7 : 5. If 9 litres of mixture is replaced by 9 liters of liquid B, then the ratio of the two liquids becomes 7 : 9. How much of the liquid A was there in the bucket ?
s: Suppose the can initially contains 7x and 5x litres of mixtures A and B respectively. When 9 litres of mixture are drawn off, quantity of A in mixture left: $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {7x - {\frac{7}{{12}}} \times 9} \right]\, \text{litres} \\ & = \left[ {7x - {\frac{{21}}{4}} } \right]\,{\text{litres}} \\ & {\text{Similarly quantity of B in mixture left}}, \\ & = \left[ {5x - {\frac{5}{{12}}} \times 9} \right]\, \text{litres} \\ & = \left[ {5x - {\frac{{15}}{4}} } \right]\,{\text{litres}} \\ & \therefore \,{\text{ratio becomes}}, \\ & \frac{{ {7x - {\frac{{21}}{4}} } }}{{ {\left(5x - {\frac{{15}}{4}}\right)+9 } }} = \frac{7}{9} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{ {28x - 21} }}{{ {20x + 21} }} = \frac{7}{9} \\ & \Rightarrow {252x - 189} = 140x + 147 \\ & \Rightarrow 112x = 336 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 3 \\ & {\text{So the can contained}}, \\ & = 7 \times x \\ & = 7 \times 3 \\ & = 21\,{\text{litres of A initially}}{\text{.}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A bucket contains a mixture of two liquids A & B in the proportion 5 : 3. If 16 litres of the mixture is replaced by 16 litres of liquid B, then the ratio of the two liquids becomes 3 : 5. How much of the liquid B was there in the bucket?
s: Let bucket contains 5x and 3x of liquids A and B respectively. When 16 litres of mixture are drawn off, quantity of A in mixture left: $$\begin{aligned} & {5x - {\frac{5}{8}} \times 16} = {5x - 10} \\ & {\text{Similarly quantity of B in mixture left}}, \\ & {3x - {\frac{3}{8}} \times 16} = {3x - 6} \\ & {\text{Now the ratio becomes,}} \\ & \frac{{ {5x - 10} }}{{ {3x - 6} }} = \frac{3}{5} \\ & \Rightarrow 25x - 50 = 9x - 18 \\ & \Rightarrow 16x = 32 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 2 \\ & {\text{So, quantity of liquid B initially}}, \\ & = 3 \times 2 = 6\,{\text{litres}} \end{aligned}$$

q: 8 litres are drawn from a cask filled with wine and is then filled with water. This operation is performed three more times. The ratio of the quantity of wine now left in cask to that of the total solution is 16 : 81. How much wine did the cask hold originally?
s: Let the quantity of the wine in the cask originally be x litres. Using formula: Final Amount of solute that is not replaced = Initial Amount × $${\left( {\frac{{{\text{Vol}}{\text{. after removal}}}}{{{\text{Vol}}{\text{. after replacing}}}}} \right)^{\text{N}}}$$ Where N = No. of operation done. Then ratio of wine to total solution in cask after 4 operations, $$\begin{aligned} & 1 \times { {\left( {\frac{{x - 8}}{x}} \right)} ^4} = \frac{{16}}{{81}} \\ & \Rightarrow 1 \times {\left\{ {\frac{{ {x - 8} }}{x}} \right\}^4} = {\left( {\frac{2}{3}} \right)^4} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{ {x - 8} }}{x} = \frac{2}{3} \\ & \Rightarrow 3x - 24 = 2x \\ & \Rightarrow x = 24\,{\text{litres}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The milk and water in a mixture are in the ratio 7 : 5. When 15 liters of water are added to it, the ratio of milk and water in the new mixture becomes 7 : 8. The total quantity of water in the new mixture is:
s: Milk : Water 7 : 5 7 : 8 3 unit ∴ Remember water is added and not milk, so make milk equal but here milk is already equal 3 units = 15 litres 1 units = 5 litres 8 units = 40 litres Total quantity of water in the new mixture = 40 litres

q: If x : y = 5 : 2, then (8x + 9y) : (8x + 2y) is :
s: $$\frac{{\text{x}}}{{\text{y}}} = \frac{5}{2}$$ Means x = 5, y = 2 Putting value of x and y in expression 8 × 5 + 9 × 2 = 58 8 × 5 + 2 × 2 = 44 58 : 44 = 29 : 22

q: Tom is chasing Jerry. In the same interval of time Tom jumps 8 times while Jerry jumps 6 times. But the distance covered by Tom in 7 Jumps is equal to the distance covered by Jerry in 5 Jumps. The ratio of speed of Tom and Jerry is:
s: Given; 7 jumps of Tom = 5 jumps of Jerry Or, $$\frac{{{\text{Tom}}}}{{{\text{Jerry}}}} = \frac{5}{7}$$ Let Jerry's 1 leap = 7 meter and Tom's 1 leap = 5 meter Then, ratio of speed of Tom and Jerry = $$\frac{{8 \times 5}}{{6 \times 7}}$$ = $$\frac{{40}}{{42}}$$ = 20 : 21

q: The ratio of ducks and frogs in a pond is 37 : 39 respectively. The average number of ducks and frogs in the pond is 152. What is the number of frogs in the pond ?
s: Ratio of Ducks and Frogs in Pond = 37 : 39 Average of Ducks and Frogs in Pond = 152 So, total number of Ducks and Frogs in the Pond = 2 × 152 = 304 ∴ Number of Frogs = $$\frac{{304 \times 39}}{{76}}$$ = 156

q: Number of students in institutes A and B were in the ratio of 7 : 15 respectively in 2012. In 2013, the number of students in institute A increased by 25% and number of students in institutes B increased by 26%, then what was the respective ratio between number of students in institutes A and B?
s: Ratio of students in 2012 in institutes A and B = 7 : 15 Let number of students in institute A in 2012 = 700 And Number of students in institutes B in 2012 = 1500 25% increase in the number of students in 2013 Now, number of students in Institute A = 700 + 25% of 700 = 875 Number of students in B in 2013 as 26% students increased in B = 1500 + 26% of 1500 = 1890 Current Ratio of the students, $$= \frac{{875}}{{1890}} = 25:54$$

q: A and B together have Rs. 1210. If $$\frac{4}{{15}}$$ of A's amount is equal to $$\frac{2}{{5}}$$ of B's amount, how much amount does B have?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{4}{{15}}A = \frac{2}{5}B \\ & \Rightarrow A = \left( {\frac{2}{5} \times \frac{{15}}{4}} \right)B \\ & \Rightarrow A = \frac{3}{2}B \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{A}{B} = \frac{3}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow A:B = 3:2. \\ & \therefore {\text{B's}}\,{\text{share}} = Rs.\left( {1210 \times \frac{2}{5}} \right) \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = Rs.\,484 \end{aligned}$$

q: Two numbers are respectively 20% and 50% more than a third number. The ratio of the two numbers is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{third}}\,{\text{number}}\,{\text{be}}\,x \\ & {\text{Then,}}\,{\text{first}}\,{\text{number}} \\ & = 120\% \,{\text{of}}\,x = \frac{{120x}}{{100}} = \frac{{6x}}{5} \\ & {\text{Second}}\,{\text{number}} \\ & = 150\% \,{\text{of}}\,x = \frac{{150x}}{{100}} = \frac{{3x}}{2} \\ & \therefore {\text{Ratio}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{first}}\,{\text{two}}\,{\text{numbers}} \\ & = {\frac{{6x}}{5}:\frac{{3x}}{2}} = 12x:15x = 4:5 \end{aligned}$$

q: A sum of money is to be distributed among A, B, C, D in the proportion of 5 : 2 : 4 : 3. If C gets Rs. 1000 more than D, what is B's share?
s: Let the shares of A, B, C and D be Rs. 5x, Rs. 2x, Rs. 4x and Rs. 3x respectively Then, 4x - 3x = 1000 ⇒ x = 1000 ∴ B's share = Rs. 2x = Rs. (2 x 1000) = Rs. 2000

q: Seats for Mathematics, Physics and Biology in a school are in the ratio 5 : 7 : 8. There is a proposal to increase these seats by 40%, 50% and 75% respectively. What will be the ratio of increased seats?
s: Originally, let the number of seats for Mathematics, Physics and Biology be 5x, 7x and 8x respectively Number of increased seats are (140% of 5x), (150% of 7x) and (175% of 8x) $$= \left( {\frac{{140}}{{100}} \times 5x} \right),$$ $$\left( {\frac{{150}}{{100}} \times 7x} \right)$$ and $$\left( {\frac{{175}}{{100}} \times 8x} \right)$$ $$\begin{aligned} & = 7x,\,\,\frac{{21x}}{2}{\text{ and }}14x \\ & \therefore {\text{The required ratio}} \\ & = 7x:\frac{{21x}}{2}:14x \\ & = 14x:21x:28x \\ & = 2:3:4 \end{aligned}$$

q: In a mixture 60 litres, the ratio of milk and water 2 : 1. If this ratio is to be 1 : 2, then the quanity of water to be further added is:
s: Quantity of milk $$= \left( {60 \times \frac{2}{3}} \right)\,{\text{litres}} = 40\,{\text{litres}}$$ Quantity of water in it = (60 - 40) litres = 20 litres New ratio = 1 : 2 Let quantity of water to be added further be x litres $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Then,}}\,{\text{milk : water}} = {\frac{{40}}{{20 + x}}} \\ & {\text{Now}},\, {\frac{{40}}{{20 + x}}} = \frac{1}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow 20 + x = 80 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 60 \\ & \therefore {\text{Quantity}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{water}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{be}}\,{\text{added = 60}}\,{\text{litres}}{\text{.}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The ratio of the number of boys and girls in a college is 7 : 8. If the percentage increase in the number of boys and girls be 20% and 10% respectively, what will be the new ratio?
s: Originally, let the number of boys and girls in the college be 7x and 8x respectively Their increased number is (120% of 7x) and (110% of 8x) $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \left( {\frac{{120}}{{100}} \times 7x} \right)\,{\text{and}}\,\left( {\frac{{110}}{{100}} \times 8x} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{42x}}{5}\,{\text{and}}\,\frac{{44x}}{5} \\ & \therefore {\text{The}}\,{\text{required}}\,{\text{ration}} \\ & = {\frac{{42x}}{5}:\frac{{44x}}{5}} \\ & = 21:22 \end{aligned}$$

q: Salaries of Ravi and Sumit are in the ratio 2 : 3. If the salary of each is increased by Rs. 4000, the new ratio becomes 40 : 57. What is Sumit's salary?
s: Let the original salaries of Ravi and Sumit be Rs. 2x and Rs. 3x respectively $${\text{Then}},\,\frac{{2x + 4000}}{{3x + 4000}} = \frac{{40}}{{57}}$$ ⇒ 57(2x + 4000) = 40(3x + 4000) ⇒ 6x = 68,000 ⇒ 3x = 34,000 Sumit's present salary = (3x + 4000) = Rs. (34000 + 4000) = Rs. 38,000

q: If 0.75 : x :: 5 : 8, then x is equal to:

q: The sum of three numbers is 98. If the ratio of the first to second is 2 :3 and that of the second to the third is 5 : 8, then the second number is:

q: Two number are in the ratio 3 : 5. If 9 is subtracted from each, the new numbers are in the ratio 12 : 23. The smaller number is:

q: In a bag, there are coins of 25 p, 10 p and 5 p in the ratio of 1 : 2 : 3. If there is Rs. 30 in all, how many 5 p coins are there?
s: Let the number of 25 p, 10 p and 5 p coins be x, 2x, 3x respectively Then, sum of their values $$\begin{aligned} & = Rs.\,\left( {\frac{{25x}}{{100}} + \frac{{10 \times 2x}}{{100}} + \frac{{5 \times 3x}}{{100}}} \right) \\ & = Rs.\,\frac{{60x}}{{100}} \\ & \therefore \frac{{60x}}{{100}} = 30 \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{30 \times 100}}{{60}} = 50 \\ & {\text{Hence,}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{number}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{5p}}\,{\text{coins}} \\ & = \left( {3 \times 50} \right) \\ & = 150 \end{aligned}$$
